title: Roof Leak Repair: How to Spot and Fix Water Damage in Charlotte
excerpt: Water stains on your ceiling? Learn common leak causes, where they start, and how to fix them before costly damage occurs.
content:
Where Leaks Start

Most roof leaks don't come from a hole in shingles. They come from where things meet: where the roof meets the chimney, where a vent sticks through, where two roof planes intersect. These "flashings" are metal trim that's supposed to seal the gap. If the sealant cracks or the flashing rusts, water finds its way in.

Early Signs (Before Water Inside)

  • Granules in gutters: Asphalt shingles shed granules as they age.
  • Sagging spots: A dip in the roofline means water's pooling.
  • Moss or algae: Common in Charlotte's humidity.
  • Lifted shingles: Wind or age can lift the edges.

Repair Costs

Small patch (isolated shingle damage): $250-400. Flashing replacement: $450-850 per penetration. Larger leak with interior damage: $800-2,000.
keywords: roof leak repair Charlotte, water damage, ceiling stains

title: Hail Damage Roof Repair: What Charlotte Homeowners Need to Know
excerpt: Charlotte gets 14-20 hail events per year. Learn how to identify hail damage, file insurance claims, and get contractor quotes.
content:
How Hail Damages Roofs

Hail comes in different sizes. Pea-sized hail usually bounces off. Quarter-sized (and larger) hail dents asphalt shingles, cracks metal, and loosens the protective granules on asphalt. Each dent is a weak spot where the tar binding breaks.

What Hail Damage Looks Like

Get in the attic or look at roof photos during the sun. Hail damage shows as round dents—not gouges or cracks. The dent is darker because the protective granules are gone.

File the Insurance Claim

Most homeowners insurance covers sudden hail damage. Call your insurer within 30 days of the storm. Timeline: Day 1 call, Day 2-5 adjuster schedules, Day 5-10 inspection and estimate, Day 10-14 approval and check.
keywords: hail damage roof, storm repair Charlotte, insurance claim

title: Emergency Roof Repair: What to Do When Your Roof Fails
excerpt: A branch through your roof. A hole from hail. Water pouring in. Here's exactly what to do in the first 30 minutes.
content:
First 30 Minutes: Stop the Water

Move furniture and valuables away from the leak. Put down buckets, towels, tarps. Open windows for airflow. If there's standing water on the ceiling, use a small hole to drain it.

First 2 Hours: Call a Roofer

Yes, it's evening or weekend. Real emergency contractors work 24/7 in Charlotte. Call immediately. A contractor with availability can often place a tarp over the damage same-day—that prevents another rain from making it worse. Cost: $200-500 for emergency tarp placement.

Document Everything

Take photos and videos from inside and outside. Show the water damage and structural damage. Write down the time and what caused it. Insurance likes to see that you took action.
keywords: emergency roof repair Charlotte, same day service

title: Storm Damage Checklist: How to Inspect Your Roof After Severe Weather
excerpt: A storm just hit. Your roof's been through it. Here's your room-by-room inspection checklist before you call insurance.
content:
Inside Your Home: Signs of Roof Damage

Check ceilings and walls for water stains (fresh spots, not old ones). Look in corners and along edges where roof meets walls. Check attic insulation for wet spots. Smell for musty odors. Look at light fixtures—water around them suggests leak above.

From the Ground: Visual Roof Inspection

Use binoculars from the ground. Check for: Missing shingles, Curled or lifted shingles, Dents in the roof (hail damage), Debris on the roof, Damaged gutters or downspouts, Damaged flashing.

In the Gutters

Look at what's in them: Granules (sand-like material) = shingle damage. Debris from roof penetrations. Gutters themselves bent or pulled away.
keywords: storm damage checklist, roof inspection guide

title: Filing Insurance Claims for Roof Damage: Charlotte Guide
excerpt: Your roof's damaged. Your insurance covers it. Navigate the claim process with our step-by-step timeline and documentation tips.
content:
Step 1: Call Your Insurer (Within 24-30 Hours)

Have your policy number handy. Describe the damage, when it happened, and what caused it. Be factual. Insurance will assign a claim number and adjuster.

Step 2: Document Everything

Photos and video are your evidence. Take them fresh, same day or next day. Document exterior damage, interior damage, and close-ups of specific damage.

Step 3: Get a Contractor Estimate

Insurance wants verification. Have a local roofer assess and provide a detailed estimate. If they low-ball you, the contractor's estimate is your evidence to dispute.

The Claim Timeline

Day 1: Call, get claim number. Day 2-5: Adjuster schedules inspection. Day 5-10: Adjuster visits, estimates damage. Day 10-14: Approval and check arrives.
keywords: homeowners insurance claim, roof damage claim

title: Roof Replacement Cost: What You'll Pay in Charlotte
excerpt: Your roof's at end-of-life. Insurance declined to repair. Here's what replacement costs and what affects the price.
content:
Asphalt Shingle Roof

Average Cost: $6,000 - $12,000 for a typical 2,000 sq ft home. Price per square foot: $3-6 installed. Asphalt is the cheapest and most common. You're getting a 15-20 year roof in Charlotte's climate.

Metal Roof

Average Cost: $15,000 - $30,000 for the same 2,000 sq ft home. Price per square foot: $8-15 installed. Metal costs 2-3x more upfront but lasts 40-50 years.

What Affects the Price?

Roof pitch (steepness), Roof complexity (gables, valleys, skylights), Old material removal, Decking damage, Ventilation upgrades, Timing (spring/summer vs winter).
keywords: roof replacement cost, roofing prices Charlotte

title: Missing Shingles: Quick Repair Guide for Charlotte Homeowners
excerpt: One, three, or a dozen shingles gone. Whether it's wind, age, or debris, missing shingles need replacing fast.
content:
Why Shingles Go Missing

Wind lifts shingles, especially at edges. Age causes adhesive failure. Debris and impacts tear shingles right off. Poor installation means under-nailed shingles come loose first.

How Bad Is It?

A few missing shingles: Patch repair, $300-600. A contractor replaces the damaged shingles and seals them down. Missing shingles across a whole roof section: Your roof's at end-of-life. Consider replacement estimates.

Temporary Fix (Until Contractor Arrives)

Don't go on the roof if you're not comfortable. Put a tarp over the area or use roofing tape to seal open spots. It'll hold for a few days, but it's not permanent.

title: Metal vs Asphalt Roofing: Which Should You Choose for Charlotte?
excerpt: Two main options: asphalt (cheaper) or metal (lasts longer). Here's how to decide based on cost, durability, and hail resistance.
content:
Asphalt: The Standard Choice

Pros: Cheap upfront, familiar, wide color options, quiet, easy to repair spot damage. Cons: Short lifespan in Charlotte's heat, hail damage is expensive, needs cleaning every few years.

Metal: The Long-Term Play

Pros: Lasts 40-50 years, survives hail, minimal maintenance, energy efficient, recyclable. Cons: 2-3x more expensive, can be noisy in rain, limited color options, requires specialized contractors.

The Charlotte Factor: Hail

We get 14-20 hail events per year. Asphalt gets hammered. Metal takes dents but doesn't leak. If you're in Charlotte 10+ years, metal's ROI makes sense.
keywords: metal vs asphalt roof, roofing material comparison

title: How Long Does a Roof Last in Charlotte?
excerpt: Your roof's 12 years old. Is it still good? When do you replace it? In Charlotte, climate matters more than anywhere else.
content:
Asphalt Shingles: 12-18 Years in Charlotte

Manufacturer claim: 20-25 years. Charlotte reality: 12-18 years. The heat and humidity here break down the tar binding asphalt shingles.

Metal Roofing: 40-50 Years

Metal holds up. Charlotte's heat doesn't break it down. Hail dents it but doesn't crack it. You're looking at 40-50 years.

Signs Your Roof is Aging

Shingles curling at edges (year 10-12), Granule loss, Leaks appearing, Moss or algae growth, Sagging sections.

Timeline to Replacement

Under 10 years: Fine. 10-12 years: Start quotes. 12-15 years: Professional inspection due. 15+ years: Replacement due.
keywords: roof lifespan, how long roofs last, replacement timeline

title: Ice Dams & Snow Melt Water Damage in Charlotte
excerpt: Charlotte rarely gets heavy snow. When it does, combined with freeze-thaw cycles, water gets trapped. Here's what to watch for.
content:
How Ice Dams Form

Snow sits on your roof. Your attic is warm (from heating), so the snow melts from underneath. Meltwater runs down your roof but refreezes at the eaves (which are colder). Water backs up under your shingles. That's an ice dam.

Signs of Ice Dam Damage

Water stains on exterior walls below the roof line, Wet insulation in attic (after spring thaw), Peeling paint inside near ceilings, Musty smell (mold from water), Ice buildup on gutters.

Prevention

Good attic ventilation and insulation. Make sure your attic isn't too warm. Clear gutters completely before winter. Trim overhanging branches. Check attic ventilation isn't blocked.
keywords: ice dams, snow melt water damage, winter roof damage
